rules: PUBLIC receives no application privilege on any schema, table or function.
No runtime role holds CREATE on any schema, or TRUNCATE, REFERENCES or TRIGGER on any table - runtime roles have no DDL privilege.
No runtime role is a member of any other role, and no runtime path issues SET ROLE.
minos_migrate is the only DDL-capable LOGIN role.
minos_owner is NOLOGIN, owns every object, and is the definer of every SECURITY DEFINER function.
minos_runner holds SELECT and nothing else on experiments.experiment_jobs: every job mutation goes through a SECURITY DEFINER function.
evaluation.truth_bindings is readable by minos_evaluator alone - the verifier, which otherwise reads every table, is deliberately excluded.

audit_contract.actor_identity: session_user - the INVOKING login identity - is recorded, never current_user. Every audited function is SECURITY DEFINER, so current_user is always the definer principal and would make every row look identical.

admin_operations.evidence_hash: sha256 of the recovery set's recovery_manifest_sha256, in lowercase hex; it points at the exact recovery evidence the operation was authorized by
admin_operations.rule: Written in the SAME transaction as the backup_sets INSERT, so a failed or rolled-back registration leaves no admin row.

audit_contract.atomicity: Every audit row is written inside the caller's transaction. A rollback, a constraint violation or a failed gate leaves no audit row at all - there is no out-of-band logging path.
audit_contract.evidence_hash_formula: payload_hash = encode(sha256(convert_to(jsonb_build_object(...)::text, 'UTF8')), 'hex'). The evidence is a jsonb object naming every immutable field relevant to the operation, so the preimage is unambiguous - delimiter-joined strings collide, since 'a:b' || ':' || 'c' and 'a' || ':' || 'b:c' are the same bytes. jsonb normalises key order, so the text form is deterministic for a given value.
audit_contract.no_op_rule: An idempotent replay that changes nothing writes NO event. Exactly one event per actual successful state change is the invariant, and the tests assert the count, not the presence.
audit_contract.non_state_changing_observations: catalog.record_artifact_verification() called when the observation does not change verification_state refreshes last_verified_at and writes NO event. That is classified here, deliberately: a timestamp refresh is an observation, not a state change, and the invariant the tests assert is exactly one event per ACTUAL change.

no_delete_tables.note: Every DB-V2 table refuses DELETE. History is superseded, never removed; retention is a separately authorized administrative operation, not a runtime capability.

role_provisioning.database_privilege_note: CREATE on the database is a database-level privilege, so migration 0009 VERIFIES it and never grants it: granting it would be a database-level privilege change, which D2 does not make. The operational provisioning step grants CREATE ON DATABASE to the definer principal before the migration runs, and 0009 fails closed until it has.

digest_basis.artifact_snapshot_manifest: content_sha256 = sha256(DOMAIN_bytes || manifest_bytes), the domain-separated aggregate digest declared in artifact_snapshot_digest
digest_basis.note: The two recovery documents digest differently ON PURPOSE: the domain prefix makes an artifact-snapshot digest unusable as a recovery-manifest digest even if the two documents ever serialize identically.
digest_basis.recovery_manifest: content_sha256 = sha256(manifest_bytes), with no domain prefix

role_provisioning.downgrade_rule: Downgrading 0009 drops DB-V2 objects only. It NEVER drops, alters or revokes a cluster role: roles outlive the migration that used them, and a downgrade that removed them would break every other database in the cluster that shares them.

elevation.deelevation_note: The migration's last statement returns the connection to the original identity, because Alembic updates public.alembic_version inside this same transaction AFTER the body, and the definer principal deliberately holds no privilege on that shared table. This is scoping, not the safety boundary: SET LOCAL is what guarantees no elevated session survives an abort, and an abort before this statement still leaves nothing elevated.
elevation.why_local: SET LOCAL is bounded by the transaction. SET ROLE outlives it and would leave the pooled connection elevated if the migration aborted between the elevation and a reset.

role_provisioning.failure_mode: If any required role is absent, is not a role, has the wrong LOGIN/NOLOGIN configuration, carries SUPERUSER, CREATEROLE or CREATEDB, or if the migration identity is not a member of the definer principal, migration 0009 raises BEFORE the first CREATE, ALTER or GRANT statement and before the elevation. The transaction aborts with nothing created.
role_provisioning.migration_session_role: The migration elevates with SET LOCAL ROLE minos_owner - never SET ROLE - and only AFTER the whole preflight has passed. SET LOCAL is transaction-scoped: the elevation is undone automatically when the transaction commits or aborts, so no RESET ROLE is needed and none is issued. Not needing a manual reset IS the safety boundary: a migration that crashes between SET ROLE and RESET ROLE would otherwise leave an elevated session behind. No runtime path issues SET ROLE or SET LOCAL ROLE at all.
role_provisioning.no_credentials: No password, credential, DSN or secret appears in any migration, report or test. Roles are provisioned outside the migration, and their authentication is a cluster concern.
role_provisioning.operational_provisioning: A future operational provisioning step - authorized separately, and NOT part of 0009 - creates or verifies the required cluster roles before the migration runs.
preflight_order: on the ORIGINAL migration identity, record session_user and current_user
verify every required role exists in pg_roles
verify every required role has its declared LOGIN/NOLOGIN and attribute configuration
verify the migration identity has membership in the NOLOGIN definer principal
verify no required role has SUPERUSER, CREATEROLE or CREATEDB
verify the definer principal may create schemas in this database
only after every check passes: SET LOCAL ROLE minos_owner
re-check current_user and require it to equal the definer principal
only then: CREATE SCHEMA and every DB-V2 object
only then: apply the D2 physical ACL matrix
finally: SET LOCAL ROLE NONE, so Alembic's own version update runs as the original identity
role_provisioning.role_attribute_contract_note: The preflight enforces exactly this table: LOGIN for the eight service identities, NOLOGIN for the definer principal, membership of the migration identity in the definer principal, and the absence of SUPERUSER, CREATEROLE and CREATEDB on all nine. It does not create, alter or drop any of them. The V1 migration 0001 created four of these names NOLOGIN for its own use; an operational provisioning step must bring them to this configuration BEFORE 0009 runs, and 0009 fails closed until it has.
role_provisioning.roles_are_cluster_scoped: PostgreSQL roles are cluster objects, not database-local ones. Migration 0009 therefore does NOT create login roles or passwords - it preflights them and fails closed if they are absent or incompatible.
role_provisioning.scratch_test_rule: Scratch-database tests provision the required roles before invoking Alembic, so the preflight passes on a throwaway cluster exactly as it would in operations.

storage_mode_contract.note: catalog.enforce_backup_set_shape() recomputes the recovery manifest and artifact-snapshot manifest digests from their bytes, so those two artifacts must be stored inline (storage_mode = 'inline', bounded by ck_artifacts_inline_bounded). A database dump is never inline. Without this the gate could only re-check the composite foreign key, not the bytes, and conditions 7 to 13 would be unenforceable.

active_selection_window.forbidden_rule: effective_to is set exactly once, never cleared and never moved; a closed selection window is history. At most one open window per selection scope.

artifact_lifecycle.forbidden_rule: deleted and quarantined are terminal; nothing returns to 'active'.

artifact_location.additional_rule: At most one location per artifact may carry is_primary = true, and a location may only be primary while it is 'present'. A location that stops being present loses its primary flag in the same statement. Returning to 'present' is permitted only through a successful catalog.record_artifact_verification() of the correct bytes.
artifact_location.forbidden_rule: Evacuation is terminal: those bytes are gone from that backend and a replacement copy is a new artifact_locations row. 'missing' and 'corrupt' are observations, not sentences - a restored payload may return the location to 'present', but only through a verification that matched the artifact's immutable digest and size.

artifact_verification.additional_rule: first_verified_at is set exactly once, on the FIRST transition to 'verified', and is immutable thereafter; last_verified_at only ever moves forward. A return to 'verified' is permitted only when catalog.record_artifact_verification() observed a digest AND a byte size equal to the artifact's immutable identity - the identity itself never changes, so 'verified' means 'the bytes match what this row has always claimed'.
artifact_verification.forbidden_rule: Nothing returns to 'unverified': once an observation has been made, the column records the LATEST observation, and 'never observed' is not something a row can become again. Every other move is a legitimate observation and is allowed, including recovery back to 'verified' after a restore - but only through record_artifact_verification(), which requires the observed digest and size to match.

attempt_exclusivity.forbidden_rule: One attempt has EITHER exactly one execution_results row OR exactly one execution_failures row, never both and never two of either. The pair of triggers checks the opposite table under the attempt row's lock, so a concurrent insert of the other kind cannot slip between the check and the insert.

attempt_outcome.additional_rule: finished_at, runtime_ms, gatk_executable_sha256 and gatk_version are NULL while outcome IS NULL and are set, together, exactly once, on the terminal transition. finished_at must be >= started_at.
attempt_outcome.forbidden_rule: An attempt's outcome is written exactly once and never rewritten, and never cleared back to NULL.

audit_append_only.forbidden_rule: audit.events and audit.admin_operations accept INSERT only. No role, including the definer principal, may UPDATE or DELETE an audit row; correction is a new row.

backup_set_immutability.forbidden_rule: completeness is immutable. A database_only row is never upgraded in place; a later complete capture receives a new recovery_set_id and backup_key.

evaluation_run_state.additional_rule: completed_at is set exactly once, with the terminal transition.
evaluation_run_state.forbidden_rule: A finished evaluation run is never restarted in place, and a run never completes without having been 'running'.

job_state.additional_rule: CLAIMED -> PENDING and RUNNING -> PENDING are the lease-expiry release path only: each requires lease_expires_at < now(), clears claimed_by, claimed_at and lease_expires_at (which ck_jobs_claim_invariant then requires for PENDING), and never decreases attempt_count. attempt_count is monotonic. terminal_attempt_id is set exactly once, on the transition to a terminal state, and must reference an attempt of this exact job through uq_attempts_id_job.
job_state.forbidden_rule: A terminal job never reopens, and a job never reaches a terminal state without passing through RUNNING - the attempt that produced the outcome must exist. PENDING may not jump straight to RUNNING: the claim is what creates the lease.

lease_transition.forbidden_rule: fence_token is strictly monotonic across every UPDATE, so a stale holder's fenced write is always detectable. A different holder may take the lease only once expires_at <= now(); the same holder may renew at any time. acquired_at changes only when the holder changes, and expires_at never moves backwards for the same holder.

model_activation.additional_rule: At most one activation row per activation scope may have deactivated_at IS NULL, enforced by a partial unique index and re-checked under the scope row's lock.
model_activation.forbidden_rule: A deactivated activation is never reactivated: deactivated_at is set exactly once and never cleared. Re-activating a model version inserts a new activation row.

profile_snapshot_state.forbidden_rule: A snapshot is born frozen - its membership and snapshot_hash are fixed at insert - and supersession is terminal. A superseded snapshot never returns to 'frozen'.

release_state.additional_rule: At most one release may be in state 'active', re-checked under the row lock; ix_releases_state indexes exactly that partial set.
release_state.forbidden_rule: A release reaches 'active' only through 'qualified' - it is never promoted straight from 'draft' - and a superseded release is never reactivated; a new release row is required.

service_instance_state.additional_rule: last_heartbeat_at only moves forward, and release_id may change only while the instance is 'starting'.
service_instance_state.forbidden_rule: 'stopped' is terminal; a restarted process registers a NEW instance with a new instance_key. Nothing returns to 'starting'.

training_run_state.additional_rule: completed_at is set exactly once, with the terminal transition.
training_run_state.forbidden_rule: A finished training run is never restarted in place.
